items.title: Whispering Water: Materializing Human-AI Dialogue as Interactive Ripples
items.abstract: Water has long served as a recipient of human confession across cultures. Whispering Water is an interactive installation that materializes human-AI dialogue through cymatic patterns on water. Participants confess to a water surface, triggering a four-phase ritual of confession, contemplation, response, and release. Vocal affect primes the water’s physical state, while semantic content enters a multi-agent dialogue among heterogeneous LLMs. Synthesized agent speech is decomposed and remapped into low-frequency components that drive six subwoofers, producing overlapping surface patterns. The installation explores how ritual, materiality, and machine dialogue can support sensory forms of emotional reflection.

items.title: Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI
items.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable embodied artificial intelligence (AI) by translating visual observations and language instructions into robotic actions. Emerging use cases in physical AI are expected to drive the need for efficient inference and communication, as the computational demands of the VLA models pose challenges for real-time control with limited onboard resources. Test-time scaling through latent reasoning allows these models to refine hidden representations without generating explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens, but introduces a trade-off between task success, inference latency, and energy consumption. In this paper, we address the efficient collaborative inference under a realistic communication scenario. We propose a wireless edge-assisted framework for adaptive latent reasoning (WEALR) that augments onboard computation with edge computing. A decision-making agent jointly selects the execution location and latent-reasoning convergence threshold. We formulate this joint adaptation as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). A Lagrangian-constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) approach, namely trust region policy optimization Lagrangian (TRPO-Lag), learns to balance task performance and resource consumption under varying wireless conditions and task requirements. We evaluate the framework using LIBERO manipulation tasks, profiled VLA inference costs, and ray-traced wireless channels. Experimental results demonstrate that TRPO-Lag achieves up to 23% higher feasibility-weighted task success rate compared to benchmark CDRL methods.

items.title: Workforce diversity and employee performance: Talent management and innovation as strategic catalysts
items.abstract: This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesizes contemporary research by examining the relationship between workforce diversity and employee performance. This review also aims to synthesize the current literature to examine how talent management and innovation act as strategic catalysts, transforming workforce diversity into measurable organizational excellence. This review integrates four complementary analytical approaches using a structured and rigorous design. First, a systematic search and screening process guided by the PRISMA framework identified relevant studies published between 2010 and 2025 from Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and major academic publishers. Second, descriptive and trend analyses were performed to examine publication growth, geographic distribution, journal quality, and dominant research context. Third, thematic analysis identified recurring themes, theoretical perspectives, and conceptual linkages between workforce diversity, talent management, workplace innovation, and employee performance. Finally, a content analysis synthesized the empirical findings to clarify the mediating and contextual mechanisms across the selected studies. Following the PRISMA process, 42 high-quality empirical and conceptual articles were included in the final review. The findings revealed a steady growth in diversity-performance research since 2010, with a significant shift after 2015 from direct effects models toward mechanism-based explanations. In general, workforce diversity rarely has a direct effect on employee performance; instead, its effect is largely indirect and dependent on supportive organizational practices. Inclusive and strategic talent management mediates this relationship by enabling the equitable recruitment, development, and retention of diverse human resources, whereas workplace innovation facilitates the effective utilization of heterogeneous knowledge through participatory, adaptive, and learning-oriented work practices. This review identifies the resource-based view, social exchange theory, and sociotechnical systems theory as dominant theoretical foundations explaining how workforce diversity becomes a performance-enhancing resource when supported by appropriate managerial capabilities, leadership behaviors, and organizational systems. Despite these advances, important gaps remain, including limited integration of diversity, talent management, and workplace innovation within a single framework, overreliance on cross-sectional designs, and insufficient evidence from developing economies and vocational or educational contexts. This review proposes an integrated conceptual perspective to guide future research and organizational practice.

items.title: ‘Chucking their stuff into ChatGPT and hitting send’: AI slop in the administrative state
items.abstract: Abstract Most research on artificial intelligence (AI) in the administrative state focuses on its use by officials. This article addresses a comparatively neglected issue: the impact of the use of AI tools by the public themselves. Drawing on a qualitative survey with over 500 civil servants in the United Kingdom, it argues that AI use by the public is increasingly disrupting the front line of the administrative state. The argument is set out in three parts. First, as the administrative state increasingly relies on text‐based inputs, officials use correspondence as a proxy for individuals – a longstanding assumption of ‘autographic’ authorship that the diffusion of generative AI tools unsettles. Second, the problem can be characterized as ‘AI slop’: AI‐generated correspondence with high volume and velocity that adopts a particular voice in interactions with officials. Third, this AI slop causes three forms of disruption: to the signals that officials draw from correspondence, to trust between officials and the public, and to systems that are ill‐equipped to deal with it. The article concludes by arguing that the status quo itself fails to adequately meet the needs of many people accessing services, and that systems need to be redesigned not only for a society beset by AI slop, but also in ways that address the drivers of it.

items.title: ‘One-night community’—how karaoke bars foster social capital as urban third places
items.abstract: The aim of this study is to explore how karaoke bars, as urban third places, can foster social capital. Data were collected in three Finnish cities. The primary data comprise interviews with karaoke singers and hosts, supplemented by the researcher’s ethnographic observational materials, recordings, and field diary entries. The findings suggest that karaoke bars can be understood as important low-threshold third places in urban environments. This study contributes to urban third-place research and leisure studies by showing how temporary, low-threshold cultural encounters can be examined in relation to bridging social capital through social participation, reciprocity, and trust.

items.title: „Ég þarf ekki hrós“: Upplifun grunnskólakennara af faglegri endurgjöf og viðurkenningu í starf
items.abstract: Mikilvægi endurgjafar í starfi hefur verið áréttað í fjölmörgum rannsóknum, sérstaklega í störfum þar sem erfitt er að meta árangur með formlegum hætti. Starf grunnskólakennara byggist að stórum hluta á samskiptum, tengslum og félagslegum ferlum sem erfitt er að meta með hefðbundnum mælikvörðum. Rannsóknir benda til þess að kennarar upplifi skort á faglegri endurgjöf og að mat á störfum þeirra sé oft óskýrt. Markmið rannsóknarinnar var að varpa ljósi á upplifun grunnskólakennara af endurgjöf og viðurkenningu í starfi og auka skilning á þýðingu hennar í faglegu starfi kennara. Tekin voru hálfopin viðtöl við sextán grunnskólakennara í tólf grunnskólum í sex sveitarfélögum. Þátttakendur voru umsjónarkennarar, faggreinakennarar og sérkennarar með fjölbreytta starfsreynslu. Niðurstöðurnar sýndu að viðmælendur gerðu skýran greinarmun á hrósi annars vegar og faglegri endurgjöf hins vegar. Þótt margir teldu sig ekki þurfa hrós lögðu þeir áherslu á faglega athygli, viðurkenningu og samtal um kennsluna sjálfa. Viðbrögð nemenda gegndu einnig veigamiklu hlutverki í mati kennaranna á eigin starfi og voru mikilvæg uppspretta faglegrar viðurkenningar. Líðan, þátttaka, tengsl og dagleg viðbrögð nemenda voru meðal þeirra vísbendinga sem kennararnir notuðu við mat á eigin árangri. Um leið lýstu margir takmarkaðri reynslu af markvissri endurgjöf frá stjórnendum. Þegar slík endurgjöf átti sér stað lýstu kennarar henni sem mikilvægri fyrir sjálfstraust, starfsánægju og faglega speglun. Niðurstöðurnar benda til þess að endurgjöf felist ekki aðeins í hrósi eða jákvæðri staðfestingu á gæðum hennar heldur einnig í áhuga á kennslunni, sértækri endurgjöf og gagnvirku samtali. Framlag rannsóknarinnar felst einkum í að varpa ljósi á hvernig kennarar greina á milli hróss, faglegrar viðurkenningar og endurgjafar, auk þess að draga fram mikilvægt hlutverk viðbragða nemenda í mati kennaranna á eigin starfi. Niðurstöðurnar undirstrika mikilvægi faglegs samtals og endurgjafar í daglegu skólastarfi.

items.title: “Virtual Urbanism: An AI-driven framework for quantifying urban identity. A Tokyo-based pilot study using diffusion-generated synthetic environments”
items.abstract: Globalization and standardization erode the distinctive character of neighbourhoods, yet such distinctiveness remains challenging to quantify computationally. This paper introduces Virtual Urbanism (VU), an AI-driven framework for quantifying urban identity at neighbourhood scale. While urban studies increasingly incorporate generative AI, their analytical medium is largely two-dimensional, not spatially grounded, and too sparsely sampled to separate recurrent from incidental features. VU’s pipeline instead uses a PLATEAU-informed 3D model to condition text-to-image generation by Stable Diffusion fine-tuned with area-specific low-rank adaptation (LoRA) models, synthesising sequential urban scenes for urban perceptual studies in Japan. Nine Tokyo areas were rendered as synthetic sequences, excluding existing orientation markers to elicit core identity-forming elements through sequential repetition. Evaluation combined human-perceptual assessment with computational comparison in LoRA weight space and DINOv2 image space. Mean identification accuracy of ∼80% confirmed sequences’ perceptual validity; Urban Identity Level (UIL) metric made urban identity levels comparable; semantic analysis identified culturally embedded typologies as identity-forming elements. Weight-space and human-perceptual evidence converged independently, both isolating the corporately redeveloped areas as least distinctive, making the erosion of local character computationally tractable. VU is thus positioned as a proof-of-concept for AI-augmented urban analysis, outlining a path toward automated, multi-parameter identity metrics to guide adaptive urban transformation.

items.title: A Bio‐Inspired Binary Micro‐Structured Transparent Meta‐Film for Thermal Signature Control and Multispectral Camouflage
items.abstract: Transparent materials with thermal‐signature control characteristics are of paramount importance for both military and civilian applications, including camouflage, information encryption, and thermal management. However, challenges including intricate manufacturing processes and noticeable visual differences across different emissivities persist. Inspired by the amphiphilic structure of the Stenocara beetle, this work designed a binary microstructured meta‐film to control thermal signatures. Within the infrared spectrum, the binary microstructure exhibits distinct emissivities, creating thermal counterparts of “0” and “1” binary states for information encryption and thermal camouflage. In the visible range, the identical material composition of the binary microstructure leads to similar optical transparency. This renders them visually indistinguishable, thereby concealing the stored information. At the same time, the continuous metallic network embedded in the meta‐film retains excellent electric conductivity. These features enable compatibility with optical anti‐counterfeiting materials and responsiveness to external stimuli, making the proposed meta‐film a promising candidate for multispectral camouflage and multistimulus, multilevel information encryption technologies.

items.title: A quasi-experimental one-group pre-post test design among miner workers: relaxation using traditional Dayak Sape music
items.abstract: Background: Mine workers face elevated occupational health risks, including hypertension, work-related stress, and poor sleep quality. Non-pharmacological interventions such as music therapy offer a promising, low-cost approach to managing these conditions. Traditional Dayak Sape music, known for its soothing melodic qualities, has shown therapeutic potential in clinical settings; however, its effectiveness in occupational populations has not been studied. Methods: A quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was employed with 52 mine workers at PT X, East Kalimantan, who had prehypertension or hypertension. Participants listened to Dayak Sape music for 10 minutes every night (Monday–Friday) over 4 weeks. Blood pressure was measured using a digital sphygmomanometer, physiological stress via salivary alpha-amylase (cocoro meter), and sleep quality using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Pre- and post-test comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results: Following the 4-week intervention, all outcome variables showed statistically significant improvements (p < 0.001). Systolic blood pressure decreased from 139 ± 14.3 to 129 ± 11.9 mmHg, and diastolic blood pressure from 93.6 ± 7.69 to 88.7 ± 5.95 mmHg. Physiological stress (salivary alpha-amylase) declined from 21.2 ± 16.0 to 9.08 ± 6.85 kU/L, and sleep quality scores improved from 7.44 ± 3.49 to 5.35 ± 2.56. Effect sizes were large to very large (r = 0.743–1.000). Conclusion: Nighttime relaxation using traditional Dayak Sape music is an effective, culturally appropriate non-pharmacological intervention for reducing blood pressure, work-related physiological stress, and improving sleep quality among mine workers. Integration of this intervention into occupational health programs in the mining sector is recommended.

items.title: AI and Stress
items.abstract: Given the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) tools at work, understanding their health implications is critically important. We use rich survey data from Finland and apply propensity score matching that accounts for observable differences between regular AI users and non‐users to estimate the relationship between reported AI usage at work and workers’ reported stress. Regular AI use is associated with a 4.4 percentage point higher probability of reporting stress, equivalent to a 25.6% increase relative to baseline. Comparing two competing explanations, we find that this pattern is more consistent with heavier work demands than with concerns about job loss: AI use is associated with more unpaid work outside working hours and, less precisely, with intense work absorption, but not with job insecurity. Exploratory subgroup estimates are larger and individually significant for men, non‐supervisors, unionized workers and employees in medium‐sized workplaces, although the differences across subgroups are not statistically significant.

items.title: AI Versus Human Recommendation: Effects on Decision Switch Under Conflict
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated in everyday decision-making, understanding how individuals respond to AI versus human advice is critical. The present study examined whether individuals are more likely to revise their initial decisions based on recommendations’ source (AI vs. Human) and stance (Agree vs. Disagree), while holding recommendation content constant. Fifty-nine participants completed eight game scenarios from popular casino games. After each initial choice, participants received a recommendation and were prompted to re-make the same decision. Mixed-effects logistic regression revealed that there is a strong tendency for participants to switch their selection when presented with disagreeing recommendations, regardless of its source. No significant differences were found in switching behaviors between AI and human-disagree conditions, though confidence increased in presence of decision switch when the opposing recommendation came from AI. Future research should explore how individual differences and contextual factors influence adoption of AI advice.

items.title: AI-integrated programmatic assessment: a proposed framework for safeguarding cognitive development in AI-augmented learning environments
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has unsettled a quiet assumption on which assessment in higher education has long relied: that the work a student submits is a reasonable proxy for what that student can do. When a fluent essay or a plausible solution can be produced with little independent effort, the inference from product to competence weakens. Institutional responses have concentrated on integrity, detection, and compliance, and less on what sustained reliance on these tools may do to learning. Emerging evidence shows that performance with AI and learning without it can come apart, and we argue that the more important risk is therefore developmental: that some forms of reliance may bypass or, over time, erode the effortful thinking through which durable understanding and professional judgement are built. We treat this as a testable possibility rather than an established general effect. Building on programmatic assessment, we propose AI-Integrated Programmatic Assessment (AIPA). The model samples three streams of evidence on the same construct: unaided cognition, AI-mediated performance, and the quality with which learners orchestrate AI. It treats orchestration as a professional competence to be taught and assessed rather than a behaviour to be policed, and it specifies explicit rules for interpreting differences between what a learner can do with and without AI, including band thresholds, recurrence and corroboration requirements, and a distinction between coherent and discrepant profiles. A confirmed discrepancy is read as a hypothesis about a current competence gap that prompts further sampling and a proportionate response; the term erosion is reserved for documented decline from a comparable earlier level. We position AIPA against adjacent approaches, including programme-level secure and open assessment, process-focused and interaction-trace assessment, and linked assessment designs, illustrate it through four worked cases, and set out a research agenda to test its claims.

items.title: An overview of the literature on quiet quitting and future research directions
items.abstract: Purpose: This paper explores the "quiet quitting" phenomenon, in which employees fulfill their job duties but refrain from going beyond the basic requirements. It highlights the emergence of quiet quitting as a social phenomenon, particularly gaining prominence post-pandemic, and examines its implications for employees and organizations. The purpose is to understand the drivers behind quiet quitting and its impact on employee behavior and organizational dynamics. Methodology: The study employs a qualitative approach to investigate quiet quitting, drawing on a literature review and other sources. The study analyzed the organizational factors and individual experiences contributing to the rise of quiet quitting. It has also examined various theories, including social exchange, the psychological contract, and organizational justice, to comprehensively understand the phenomenon. Findings: Quiet quitting poses significant challenges for organizations, impacting retention, productivity, and morale. It reflects employee disengagement, often unnoticed until productivity declines. Academic interest in quiet quitting is rising, with collaborative research efforts revealing its complexities. Future studies should focus on longitudinal tracking and innovative mitigation strategies. A multifaceted approach that considers individual and organizational factors that may lead to quitting is crucial for cultivating employee well-being and productivity in the workplace. Originality: This research contributes to the existing literature by shedding light on the understudied phenomenon of quiet quitting, particularly in post-pandemic dynamics. It emphasizes the need for organizations to adapt to evolving employee expectations and suggests that addressing quiet quitting requires a nuanced understanding of its drivers and implications. By proposing to draw on established theories and develop frameworks to comprehensively explore quiet quitting, this study aims to stimulate further inquiry and contribute to evidence-based management practices.

items.title: ANALYSIS OF ACCIDENT CAUSES AMONG DUMP TRUCK DRIVERS USING THE STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING–PARTIAL LEAST SQUARES (SEM-PLS) METHOD AT PT. PUTRA MAHALONA
items.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of human factors, vehicle factors, and environmental factors on occupational accidents among dump truck drivers at PT Putra Mahalona and to determine the factor with the greatest influence on occupational accidents. A quantitative approach was employed using the Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) method, with data obtained through questionnaires, observation, interviews, and documentation involving 60 dump truck drivers as respondents. The results show that all research variables met the criteria for validity and reliability, with Average Variance Extracted (AVE) values of 0.562 for the Vehicle Factor, 0.703 for the Environmental Factor, 0.643 for the Human Factor, and 0.566 for Occupational Accidents. The R-Square value of 0.600 indicates that the Human Factor, Vehicle Factor, and Environmental Factor collectively explain 60.0% of the variation in Occupational Accidents. Partially, the Vehicle Factor had a significant effect on Occupational Accidents, with a path coefficient of -0.548, a T-Statistic of 3.633, and a P-Value of 0.000, whereas the Human Factor (coefficient -0.243, T-Statistic 1.543, P-Value 0.123) and the Environmental Factor (coefficient 0.079, T-Statistic 0.736, P-Value 0.462) showed no significant effect. These findings provide information on the factors that need to be prioritized in efforts to prevent occupational accidents in dump truck operations at PT Putra Mahalona, and indicate that the Vehicle Factor is the factor with the greatest influence on occupational accidents among dump truck drivers. Therefore, vehicle condition checks prior to use and regular maintenance need to be carried out consistently to support occupational safety.

items.title: Analysis of Construction Risks to Occupational Health andSafety in Housing Development Projects in Banjarmasin andSurrounding Areas
items.abstract: Abstract. The construction sector encompasses a multitude of operational activities that exposethe workforce to a wide array of occupational hazards, thereby rendering effective OSHmanagement an indispensable component of project execution. Residential housing projectssituated in swamp-influenced zones present particular safety challenges, including falls fromheight, impacts from falling objects, electrical perils exacerbated by wet working conditions, andinjuries arising from hand-operated and power-driven implements. This investigation wasundertaken to evaluate occupational safety risks in residential housing construction withinBanjarmasin and its surrounding areas, employing the HIRARC methodology in conjunctionwith a 5×5 Risk Matrix. Primary data were derived from field observations, responses tostructured questionnaires administered to 35 construction workers, expert validation, and acomprehensive review of pertinent regulations and scholarly literature. The analysis identified15 hazard variables distributed across five principal construction phases. One hazard wasclassified as extreme, with the remaining 14 designated as high risk. The highest risk rating(17.04) was associated with work at elevation during roof installation, indicating the pressingrequirement for immediate control action. Risk mitigation strategies were developed inaccordance with the Hierarchy of Control and validated by certified construction safetypractitioners. Recommended measures include engineering interventions, administrativeenhancements, compulsory PPE usage, routine supervision, safety education, and the consistentapplication of the SMKK framework. The implementation of these strategies is expected toreduce occupational accident rates and improve safety performance in residential housingconstruction projects.

items.title: APPLICATION OF THE NORDIC BODY MAP METHOD TO IDENTIFY MUSCULOSKELETAL COMPLAINTS AMONG FRESH FRUIT BUNCH (FFB) HARVESTERS IN NORTH LUWU
items.abstract: This study aims to identify the body segments that predominantly experience musculoskeletal complaints and determine the level of ergonomic risk among Fresh Fruit Bunch (FFB) harvesters at a smallholder oil palm plantation in Rampoang Village, Tanalili District, North Luwu Regency. This study employed a descriptive design with quantitative and qualitative approaches. The sample was determined using the Total Sampling technique, involving all five permanent harvesters. Data were collected through work posture observation and a standardized Nordic Body Map (NBM) questionnaire measuring subjective complaints across 28 body segments. The results showed that the most dominant complaints occurred in the upper neck (85%), lower back (75%), right and left upper arms (65% each), and back (60%). These complaints were associated with awkward work postures, including extreme neck hyperextension when cutting fronds and fruit at heights of 4–7 meters and extreme trunk flexion when collecting loose fruit. Based on the accumulated NBM scores, 80% of workers (4 people) were classified as having a Low Risk Level with scores ranging from 45 to 48, while 20% (1 person) were classified as having a Moderate Risk Level with a score of 55. The findings indicate that FFB harvesting activities involve physical workloads concentrated in the upper and middle parts of the body. Although the current ergonomic risk level is predominantly low to moderate, improvements in work methods and regular muscle stretching are necessary to prevent the worsening of musculoskeletal injuries in the future.

items.title: ARGUS: A Secure and Resilient Edge-Based Architecture for Multimodal Sensor Fusion in IoBT Networks with Zero Trust and Dynamic Isolation of Suspicious Nodes
items.abstract: This academic presentation examines the challenges of ensuring secure, reliable, and energy-efficient operation in Internet of Battle Things (IoBT) environments, where heterogeneous sensors, autonomous systems, and mobile nodes must exchange critical information under resource constraints, unstable connectivity, and increased exposure to cyber threats. Drawing upon a critical review and comparative synthesis of relevant scientific literature, the study introduces ARGUS, a conceptual, multi-layered Edge–Fog–Cloud architecture for secure and resilient multimodal sensor fusion. The proposed framework integrates IoBT and Internet of Digital Twins (IoDT) concepts with AI-based sensing, Zero Trust principles, continuous trust assessment, and dynamic isolation of suspicious or compromised nodes. Particular emphasis is placed on the Fog/Trust Gateway, which coordinates local data processing, anomaly detection, security policy enforcement, and the selective transmission of verified information to higher-level analytical and decision-support systems. The name ARGUS draws inspiration from Argus Panoptes, the many-eyed guardian of Greek mythology, symbolizing continuous vigilance, distributed situational awareness, and security monitoring across the infrastructure. The study further examines energy-aware and trust-aware routing, UAV-assisted data collection, network resilience, and the operational trade-offs between energy efficiency, communication performance, and security. Through a structured qualitative comparison of existing technological approaches, it highlights their complementary capabilities and limitations, positioning ARGUS as an integrated theoretical framework for future IoBT/IoDT infrastructures. Developed within the academic framework of the course “Mobile and Pervasive Computing” at the Department of Applied Informatics, University of Macedonia, this presentation offers a literature-based architectural proposal intended to support further research into secure, intelligent, and resilient distributed systems, including their potential evolution toward 2030 and beyond.

items.title: Balancing Act: A Case Study on Postgraduate Degree Pursuits by Mature Female Learners
items.abstract: This study examined how mature female learners sustained postgraduate study while working full time and raising families, a topic with few qualitative accounts in the Philippine teaching profession. Using a qualitative case study design bounded by the participants’ shared characteristics, and institutional contexts, the researchers conducted three individual semi-structured interviews and one focus group discussion with three married mothers employed as teachers in different institutional contexts. Self-Determination Theory, Feminist Theory, and the Chain of Response Model guided the interpretation of motivation, gendered constraints, and barriers to adult participation. Thematic analysis showed that participants faced time scarcity, work-related demands, financial pressure, and technological and cognitive challenges associated with age. They sustained their studies through disciplined time management, task prioritization, brief and purposeful distraction, support from family, colleagues, and administrators, and a positive attitude. Responsive and personalized academic advising emerged as a critical institutional factor that strengthened motivation, maintained momentum, and supported progress toward degree completion. Participants also valued flexible learning modalities, empathetic faculty, and structured check-ins. The findings illustrate how intrinsic motivation, resilience, and strategic coping interact with structural support to enable persistence. Interpreted through the three frameworks, participants’ needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness were supported or strained by situational, institutional, and dispositional conditions, and caregiving was redistributed among family members rather than removed. Because the case involved only three participants, the findings are offered for analytic transferability, not statistical generalization. The study recommends that higher education institutions, academic advisers, and policymakers provide flexible scheduling, financial assistance, and proactive advisory services that recognize the gendered and situational constraints faced by mature female learners.

items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Sentiment Analysis in Pregnancy-Related Weight Discussions on Reddit: Human Performance-Aligned Comparative Evaluation Study
items.abstract: Background Pregnancy-related weight gain is both physiologically complex and socially charged, and online discussions often combine clinical information with implicit emotional distress. Although automated sentiment analysis could support research on pregnancy-related discourse, model performance in this context remains inadequately characterized relative to expert human judgment. Objective This study aimed to benchmark contemporary sentiment classification models on pregnancy-related weight discussions, with emphasis on agreement with expert consensus, interpretive ambiguity, task adaptation, and deployment across posts and comments. Methods We curated 15,619 Reddit posts and comments using a large language model (LLM)–guided keyword expansion strategy and established an adjudicated consensus reference set of 200 posts. We evaluated 10 models on a fixed held-out test set (N=150) using aligned text inputs, weighted performance metrics, and 1000-resample bootstrap CIs. RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers Approach) and BERTweet (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers for Tweets) were additionally evaluated in a 5-fold fine-tuning sensitivity analysis. Gemini-3-Flash (Google DeepMind [Google LLC]) and Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT)–OSS (OpenAI) were then applied to 400 unlabeled posts and 15,019 comments with intermodel agreement assessment. To expand expert-labeled coverage, a separate 106-post annotation extension was used for secondary evaluation of the 2 models carried forward to post-level corpus inference, and cross-source recoverability of the API-derived retrieval was assessed using Arctic Shift (Arthur Heitmann). Results The 2 primary experts (FAK and BMW) achieved 59.0% preadjudication agreement (Cohen κ=0.344). In the fixed held-out comparison, Gemini-3-Flash had the numerically highest weighted F 1 -score of 0.662 (κ=0.478), followed by GPT-OSS ( F 1 -score=0.645; κ=0.436), with overlapping CIs across leading models. Under the harmonized direct-argmax decision rule with minimally processed text, BERTweet achieved an F 1 -score of 0.623 (κ=0.369), and RoBERTa achieved an F 1 -score of 0.605 (κ=0.339). In the separate fine-tuning sensitivity analysis, the mean cross-validated F 1 -score was 0.708 (SD 0.087) for RoBERTa and 0.616 (SD 0.079) for BERTweet. Among Gemini-3-Flash errors, 55.8% (29/52) occurred in posts on which the 2 primary experts disagreed. In the 106-post annotation extension, primary-expert agreement was 64.2% (68/106; κ=0.367); Gemini-3-Flash and GPT-OSS achieved weighted F 1 -score values of 0.633 and 0.680, respectively, and both identified 56 of 58 expert-negative posts in an exploratory human-review prioritization analysis. All 714 API-retrieved post IDs were independently recoverable through Arctic Shift. Intermodel agreement was 92.3% for posts (κ=0.797; n=400 valid pairs) and 46.3% for comments (κ=0.102; n=1500). Conclusions No single model architecture was uniformly superior, and performance depended on the adaptation regime, annotation ambiguity, and discourse type. These findings define important boundary conditions for sentiment analysis of naturalistic maternal-health discourse: broad polarity classification can support corpus prioritization and hypothesis generation but is insufficient as a stand-alone measure of patient experience.

items.title: Between Happiness and Success: The Contribution of Subjective Well-Being and Motivation to Academic Achievement in HSE University Students
items.abstract: In recent years, among students of leading universities, there has been an alarming dynamics of deterioration of their psychological state, which is expressed, among other things, in the suicidal behavior of students. Indicators of subjective well-being and internal motivation of students are not only at a low level, but also continue to decline with each year of study, while according to the self-determination theory, high efficiency (providing the ability to study in a highly selective university) should be supported by exactly these factors. In connection with this contradiction, the question arises: is the influence of subjective well-being and motivation on a person's success as unambiguous as it is commonly believed, or are there different profiles of motivational and emotional regulation that allow you to gain high achievements? This article is devoted to the study of the impact of the relationship between subjective well-being and various types of academic motivation on the level of academic achievements. The results of cluster and comparative analysis of the obtained data are presented. The sample of the study consisted of 209 students of bachelor's and master's degrees of various specialties of HSE. Statistical analysis showed that combinations of negative affect with extrinsic motivation and positive affect with intrinsic motivation contribute to the formation of two alternative profiles that do not affect academic success and involvement, but are reflected in the level of student well-being. It is noteworthy that the distinctive characteristics of students with high academic performance are high motivation for achievement and low negative affect. The problematic issues of well-being and motivation in the academic environment are discussed, the question of the problematic nature of external motivation in the university for the well-being of students is raised.

items.title: Between hype and uncertainty: Expert assessments of nuclear small-modular reactors (SMRs) under data center energy boom
items.abstract: The unprecedented growth in artificial intelligence and data center energy demand has renewed interest in small modular reactors (SMRs) as a potential low-carbon baseload solution. Yet significant uncertainty persists around the techno-economic characteristics and policy solutions necessary for SMR commercialization in the United States. This inadvertently leaves policymakers navigating critical decisions about resource allocation, regulatory reform, and long-term energy planning without a clear picture of near-term prospects of SMRs. This study addresses that gap by conducting a mixed methods expert survey of 33 professionals from industry, academia, government, utilities, and think tanks. Results collectively suggest a moderate confidence in an outlook with high overnight capital cost of over $6000/kW and cost overruns of over 30%, falling short of DOE's commercialization target. They also reflect cautious optimism rooted in the expectation of an incremental learning rate due to rapid electricity demand growth from data centers and standardization of design. Overall, experts highlight a significant gap between promotional narratives and realistic techno-economic trajectories.

items.title: Between the Lines: Multi-turn Contextual Investment Advice Detection
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly power financial conversational assistants, detecting investment advice in natural language has become a critical regulatory and safety challenge. Unlike explicit single-turn recommendations, investment advice often emerges implicitly and progressively over multi-turn conversations, shaped by user intent, delivery style, and contextual buildup. We introduce the first comprehensive framework for detecting both sequential and contextual investment advice in dialogue settings. Central to our approach is a modular, top-down synthetic data generation pipeline that systematically spans a taxonomy of advisory trajectories using an axis-bucket-descriptor schema. We simulate both benign and high-risk conversations across diverse user personas, financial instruments, and risk tiers, and evaluate detection capabilities using LLM-as-a-Judge with entropy-based uncertainty diagnostics. Our results show that contextual advisory detection remains substantially more challenging than sequential cases, even under few-shot prompting with tailored demonstrations. This work lays the foundation for scalable guardrail development in high-stakes, compliance-sensitive domains, where advisory risk is often subtle, distributed, and perception-dependent.

items.title: Beyond accuracy: The PRIME framework for ethical human-AI collaboration in radiology
items.abstract: Purpose Generative AI changes the radiologist's task from judging AI output to editing and signing text that AI drafted. Existing guidance covers automation bias, local validation and monitoring, but gives little direction on verifying generated text, recording its provenance, or auditing reliance on it. Approach This paper consolidates multisociety statements, consensus guidelines, human-factors evidence and the EU legal framework as of October 2026 into a practice framework, and applies it to assistive, case-allocation, autonomous and generative workflows. Framework PRIME has five principles at two levels. Primacy of accountability, rigorous verification and maintained expertise apply to the radiologist; informed transparency and earned trust through oversight apply to the institution. A recorded independent read before AI output is viewed links four principles: it serves as the omission search, keeps unassisted skill in routine work, supplies the data for reliance metrics, and documents the radiologist's own judgment. Verification is split into checking AI statements and searching for omissions. Provenance is recorded per statement and paired with local performance data. Monitoring uses an independent reference sample, because audits against the signed report miss errors that radiologists accepted. Implications Each principle names an actor, an action, an indicator and a trigger, and is mapped to the AI Act, the Medical Device Regulation, the General Data Protection Regulation and product liability law. Most rules are design proposals that still require clinical evaluation, and the framework does not resolve liability or structural inequity.

items.title: Can Voluntary Corporate Transparency Curb Corruption? Community-Level Evidence from Oil and Gas Fields in Africa
items.abstract: Voluntary corporate transparency seeks to promote accountability through disclosure, but substantive reporting does not by itself guarantee societal benefits. We examine whether this form of self-regulation can help curb corruption where formal oversight is weak, focusing on corporate support for the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI), a multistakeholder initiative that promotes disclosure of company payments to host governments. We link geolocated data on African oil and gas fields and their operators to Afrobarometer surveys and satellite nighttime-light measures and estimate difference-in-differences models that track changes in outcomes around the same fields before and after operators endorse the EITI. We find that corporate EITI support is associated with lower perceived corruption and less reported bribery, greater civic engagement, greater perceived freedom to speak, and higher nighttime-light intensity, a proxy for local economic activity. The association with lower perceived corruption is stronger around fields with nearby NGO or aid-project activity, among residents living closer to fields, and among frequent users of traditional news media. Supplementary analyses provide indirect evidence that supporting firms were more transparent before mandatory disclosure laws took effect, and show that they had fewer joint-venture partners and larger ownership stakes after endorsement. Archival cases from Nigeria and Ghana illustrate how civil-society organizations and journalists use extractive-industry information to question firms and public authorities. The findings point to local governance benefits of voluntary transparency commitments and are consistent with an information-to-accountability account in which these benefits depend on both substantive reporting and local opportunities to scrutinize and use the information.

items.title: Challenges for human oversight in detecting system malfunctions in AI-assisted medical diagnostics
items.abstract: Increasingly, physicians must oversee AI systems to detect system malfunctions. We studied 48 physicians in a randomized controlled study using an increasingly malfunctioning AI for cardiac auscultation. Diagnostic performance declined alongside AI reliability, even when physicians were cognitively forced to make an initial classification, and when human performance exceeded AI reliability. Physicians' confidence declined faster than their trust in AI. Results call for specification of oversight goals and processes ensuring patient safety.

items.title: CHOOSING AND CONSIDERING BODY SHAPES IN MODERN CLOTHING DESIGN: ARTISTIC-CONSTRUCTIVE AND SOCIO-PSYCHOLOGICAL ASPECTS
items.abstract: This article analyzes the peculiarities of choosing and considering body shapes when creating modern clothing designs, exploring its artistic-constructive and socio-psychological aspects. In the contemporary fashion industry, couturiers and designers no longer limit themselves to standard templates; instead, they focus heavily on the plasticity, proportions, and visual correction of diverse body structures. The article provides a theoretical and scientific justification for the role of lines, fabric textures, color harmony, and constructive solutions in garment design for various body types. Furthermore, it highlights the principles of creating ergonomically and aesthetically flawless garments by ensuring a harmonious balance between the consumer's individual identity and physical form. The study also considers the methodological stages of the design process, the influence of age and cultural context, the relationship between sizing systems and body morphology, and the growing importance of inclusivity and sustainability in contemporary fashion.

items.title: Cleopatra’s Motivation and Power in H. Rider Haggard’s Cleopatra
items.abstract: This article examines the motivations that drive Cleopatra to fight against her brother, Ptolemy, in H. Rider Haggard’s Cleopatra (1889). The study develops a qualitative literary analysis of the novel through close attention to dialogue, character action, political decisions, and recurring patterns of conflict. The analysis distinguishes between intrinsic motivation and power motivation and then examines how these dimensions intersect rather than operate independently. The findings identify two major intrinsic motives—desire for Egyptian independence and concern for legacy and dynastic continuity—and five major power motives: political ambition, personal rivalry, strategic calculation, manipulation and control, and personal survival. Empirical textual evidence shows that these motives are repeatedly converted into concrete political practices, including mobilizing Egyptians, preparing military forces, seeking alliances, approaching Julius Caesar, challenging Ptolemy’s legitimacy, manipulating factions, and protecting Cleopatra’s political position. The discussion demonstrates that national sovereignty and personal ambition are not mutually exclusive within the novel: Cleopatra presents the consolidation of her authority as a means of securing Egypt’s future, while her pursuit of sovereignty simultaneously strengthens her personal power. Maslow’s hierarchy of needs is employed cautiously as an interpretive framework. Recent empirical research challenges the assumption that human needs are universally satisfied in a fixed sequence, supporting a more integrated interpretation of Cleopatra’s simultaneous pursuit of security, belonging, esteem, agency, and self-realization.

items.abstract: This chapter examines the technological interface from a sociotechnical and interdisciplinary perspective.It describes the shift from the functionalist paradigm, which valued products by algorithmic performance, electronic stability and compliance with technical requirements, towards user-centred design, which holds that interactive systems must adapt to people's needs, cognitive limitations and contexts of use.Within this framework, usability and aesthetics are presented not as ornamental or independent attributes but as dimensions to be integrated.The chapter treats hardware and software as a single sociotechnical system: hardware provides the material canvas in which aesthetics first appears, while software shapes the interactive dynamics in which usability is experienced.The graphical user interface (GUI) is therefore addressed as the core of interaction, the space where functional and visual attributes converge.The approach is a conceptual, descriptive-analytical review of human-computer interaction literature, covering event-driven programming and GUI components such as icons, windows, pointing devices, menus and buttons, together with a brief historical account from Xerox PARC to the Macintosh and touchscreen devices.Drawing on this literature, the chapter states that interfaces based on visual metaphors and icons reduce the learning curve and cognitive load, and that an imbalance between hardware and software quickly undermines both aesthetics and actual usability.It concludes that a holistic, interactive approach grounded in user needs is required for products to be competitive, with user-centred design proposed as the framework for integrating usability and aesthetics in organizational settings.

items.title: Confidently Wrong: Detecting Hallucinations in Financial Question Answering from LLM Internal States
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in financial applications fail most consequentially when they are confidently wrong. Hedged, uncertain answers invite scrutiny, whereas confident errors silently degrade downstream decisions without warning. We ask how reliably such confidently wrong answers, or confident hallucinations, can be detected from a model’s internal activations, and whether those activations carry information beyond its output-level confidence signals. We train linear probes on the residual stream and evaluate them on two established numerical question-answering (QA) benchmarks built from real filings, FinQA and TAT-QA. Behavioral confidence is measured as the agreement among eight resampled answers to the same question, and probe effectiveness is compared against baselines, such as token log-probabilities and the model’s own True/False self-assessment of its answer. Our findings show that among confident answers, those for which all eight resamples agree, 15–23% are wrong on FinQA. There the probes have a significant advantage over output-level baselines in detecting hallucinations, holding 0.68–0.77 AUROC while the best baselines fall to 0.55–0.63, across Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Gemma-2-9B. Our results suggest that probing can be a cost-effective triage mechanism for routing LLM answers to human review and quality control procedures in high-stakes financial applications. Code and data are available at https://github.com/richardzhewang/confidently-wrong.

items.title: Conversational Capture: A Trajectory-Level Framework for Evaluating Generative Engine Optimization in Multi-turn Human-Agent Interaction
items.abstract: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) shapes content to increase its likelihood of being cited by answer engines built on retrieval-augmented large language models. GEO is typically evaluated as a single-turn property: for a fixed query, an evaluator measures a source’s visibility in one answer. We argue that the single answer is an inadequate unit of analysis. Human-agent information seeking forms a closed loop. The agent’s answer changes the user’s beliefs and therefore the next question, which in turn determines what the agent retrieves. We introduce conversational capture, a phenomenon in which a source cited early becomes substantially more likely to be cited again. Capture operates through a machine-side channel, history-conditioned retrieval, and a human-side channel, follow-up questions directed toward the captured source. This persistence can be independent of the source’s current relevance. We formalize the interaction as a two-layer closed-loop system and derive computable trajectory-level constructs: cumulative conversational visibility; a decomposition of trajectory gain into a single-turn "direct" term and a closed-loop "feedback" term; a nested counterfactual split of the feedback term into machine-side and human-side channels; a capture coefficient; a compounding ratio; and a misranking diagnostic. Using reinforcement-process (Pólya-urn) theory, we prove that the feedback term is identically zero under single-turn evaluation and that GEO’s cumulative payoff grows superlinearly with conversation length while capture develops. A model-derived illustration shows that the feedback term can exceed the direct term, the compounding ratio exceeds two within ten turns, and the single-turn and trajectory rankings of GEO methods agree only weakly (Kendall’s τ = 0.4). Thus, single-turn evaluation can select the wrong method. We connect the human channel to information foraging, trust calibration, and Bayesian persuasion, and discuss design implications for answer engines.

items.title: Data visualization and visual analytics as support for the investigation of document and identity fraud in the public sector
items.abstract: Verifying citizens' identities and the authenticity of documents has become a critical step in the delivery of public services, especially with the expansion of digital government and the growth of identity fraud attempts in Brazil. Much of this verification still depends on the comparison of images and records by human analysts, a task that cognitive psychology research shows to be subject to relevant error rates. This article analyzes the role of data visualization and visual analytics tools as support for the investigation of document and identity fraud in the public sector. It is a qualitative and exploratory study, based on bibliographic and documentary research, combining work on information visualization, unfamiliar face matching, cognitive load theory, visual analytics applied to fraud detection and the interaction between humans and automated systems in public administration. The analysis indicates that interfaces able to gather evidence in a single environment, support side-by-side comparison and reduce switching between systems tend to lower cognitive effort and may favor more consistent decisions. The literature also shows that combining a trained specialist with a highperforming algorithm outperforms the combination of two specialists, while warning about algorithmic bias, automation bias and harms already observed in public anti-fraud programs. The study concludes that visualization should be conceived as an instrument that amplifies human judgment, with traceable decisions and safeguards for citizens' rights.

items.title: Decoding decision correctness from EEG under high cognitive workload in virtual reality: implications for collaborative brain-computer interface teams
items.abstract: Introduction Collaborative Brain-Computer Interfaces (cBCIs) offer a promising mechanism to augment team decision‐making, but existing approaches rely exclusively on evidence available only after a decision has been made and reported, such as reaction time or stated confidence. This limits their use to explaining or discounting a decision after the fact, rather than informing a teams response before it is finalised. We tested whether spatial‐covariance EEG features could instead provide a genuinely pre-emptive signal of an operators decision correctness, available within the response window itself, and whether such a signal depends on cognitive workload. Methods Using a continuous virtual reality target-detection task, participants (N = 23) completed a within-subject visual workload manipulation (High vs. Low), implemented via a Degraded Visual Environment. Results A Riemannian tangent‐space classifier, trained on a strictly motor‐safe EEG window preceding each response, decoded Correct from Incorrect decisions with above‐chance accuracy under High Workload (61.4%, p = .0014, N = 23) but not reliably under Low Workload (N = 17), where near‐ceiling behavioural accuracy left too few error trials for valid classification. Ablation analysis showed the signal was carried predominantly by posterior occipito‐parietal channels, consistent with a perceptual rather than motor origin. At the team level, weighting votes by this pre-emptive neural signal, available before a response is committed, produced substantial accuracy gains on contested (evenly‐split) trials under High Workload (57% to 88% as team size increased from 2 to 16), but was actively detrimental under Low Workload. Discussion Critically, this advantage held even against post‐hoc behavioural signals: confidence was the strongest single team‐level signal overall, but by definition cannot inform a decision still in progress, whereas the neural signal can. These findings indicate that EEG‐based decision‐reliability signals are not a general‐purpose team augmentation tool, but a workload‐conditional one, with clear implications for when and how cBCI systems should be deployed in operational teams.

items.title: Design and Ergonomic Evaluation of an Automated Wheelchair Lifting Aid for Caregiver Injury Prevention
items.abstract: Background: Manual handling during wheelchair loading and unloading imposes substantial biomechanical demands on caregivers, potentially contributing to work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) because of non-neutral working postures and increased spinal loading, particularly at the L5/S1 lumbosacral junction. Objective: This study proposes the design, development, and ergonomic evaluation of an electromechanical assistive lifting device integrated into the cargo compartment of a Toyota Avanza multipurpose vehicle (MPV). Methods: A 12-V DC electric winch equipped with a swiveling boom arm and a quick-release sling harness was evaluated during caregiver-assisted wheelchair loading and unloading tasks involving three wheelchair configurations: a standard manual wheelchair (17 kg), a Type A powered wheelchair, and a Type B powered wheelchair (weighing up to 28 kg). Functional compatibility and observable caregiver working postures were assessed before and after device implementation. Results: Automated lifting system successfully demonstrated proof-of-concept operation with all three wheelchair configurations. Compared with manual handling, assisted loading reduced the need for non-neutral caregiver postures, including approximately 30° of backward trunk extension and approximately 75° of asymmetric lower-extremity bracing. By replacing manual lifting effort with electromechanical assistance, the device enabled the caregiver to maintain a more upright working posture during the demonstrated operations. However, repeated trial counts were not documented; therefore, no statistical success rate or quantified reduction in biomechanical loading can be established. Conclusion: Proof-of-concept device demonstrated functional feasibility and the potential to reduce non-neutral caregiver postures during wheelchair loading and unloading. Its integration into the vehicle cargo compartment offers a practical retrofit concept for assisted wheelchair transportation.

items.title: Design and Implementation of a Grid-Independent, Non-Destructive Assistive Telemetry Node for Transitory and Rental Space Accessibility
items.abstract: Conventional domestic entry notification frameworks rely predominantly on acoustic propagation, presenting an institutionalized accessibility barrier for the deaf and hard-of-hearing demographic. While localized visual or haptic retrofitting solutions exist for permanent installations, they remain highly impractical for transitory, short-term rental, or travel accommodations where structural and electrical grid modifications are legally or structurally prohibited. This paper presents a novel, grid-independent, non-destructive assistive telemetry node designed specifically for temporary or mobile spatial environments. Utilizing a RISC-V based ESP32-C3 microcontroller, the system circumvents local spatial constraints by routing hardware-interrupt-driven trigger events over an automated network captive portal directly to a secure cloud broker (Telegram Bot API). The alert payload is translated at the user's mobile endpoint into multi-modal haptic-visual feedback streams, ensuring unconstrained geographical tracking. The hardware layer is packaged inside a custom additive-manufactured Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol (PETG) enclosure optimized for rugged field mobility and tool-free deployment. Electrical characterization yields an optimized deep-sleep quiescent current floor of 7.2µA sustained via an ultra-low-power low-dropout (LDO) linear regulator stage. Empirical evaluations across eighteen distinct evaluation iterations demonstrate an overall mean end-to-end network latency of 5.86 seconds and a 100% transmission success rate, translating to a mathematically validated operational battery deployment shelf-life exceeding 14 to 16 months on standard commercial alkaline cells. Qualitative field evaluations with an assistive user cohort verify that the multi-modal notification pipeline significantly enhances situational awareness and independent living capacity without technical onboarding friction.

items.title: Design-thinking scaffolds for learner-agency-preserving AI use: effects on creative self-efficacy, cognitive flexibility, and engagement
items.abstract: Introduction Generative AI can facilitate the production of student work but may also displace learners' responsibility for problem framing, evaluation, and revision. This study examined whether design-thinking scaffolds were associated with creative self-efficacy, cognitive flexibility, and problem-solving engagement during AI-supported project learning. Methods A three-condition, four-wave quasi-experimental study included 162 undergraduates in six intact class sections (54 per condition). Non-AI project learning, ordinary GenAI use, and design-thinking-scaffolded GenAI use were compared across a four-week educational design task. Baseline-adjusted models assessed self-reported outcomes, human-coded AI-use logs, and independently rated products from 54 teams. Cluster-bootstrap analyses examined temporally ordered indirect associations and moderation by pre-intervention AI over-reliance. Results Compared with ordinary GenAI, the scaffolded condition showed higher T2 creative self-efficacy (adjusted difference = 0.33, p = 0.006), T3 cognitive flexibility (0.35, p = 0.003), and T4 engagement (0.35, p = 0.004). Mean team product quality was 20.14 in the scaffolded condition, compared with 17.62 under ordinary GenAI and 16.76 without AI. Coded prompts showed fewer answer-completion requests and more comparison, critique, and reflection. Indirect estimates via creative self-efficacy (0.07), cognitive flexibility (0.09), and their sequential pathway (0.04) had bootstrap confidence intervals excluding zero. Higher initial AI over-reliance weakened the overall engagement contrast and the two single-mediator indirect pathways, whereas the moderated-sequential index had a confidence interval including zero. Discussion The findings are consistent with agency-preserving cognitive offloading when instructional scaffolds retain student responsibility for higher-order decisions. Intact-section allocation, task-specific self-reports, and limited section-level replication preclude strong causal or general-transfer claims.

items.title: Developing and validating the human-AI collaboration competency scale
items.abstract: Fostering learners’ capacity to collaborate effectively with AI has become an important goal in education. This study aims to develop and validate the Human–AI Collaboration Competency (HACC) Scale, which can be used to assess students’ perceived competency in allocating roles and managing tasks, and sharing, coordinating, and integrating with AI through ongoing interaction to achieve a common goal. This scale includes five constructs’’: engagement, fluency, team bond, interdependence, and task regulation. Two independent samples of high school students were used to examine the factor structures: Sample 1 (n = 195) was used for exploratory factor analysis (EFA), and Sample 2 (n = 356) was used for confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). The final version of the HACC Scale consisted of 25 items loaded onto 5 factors. Construct validity was supported through EFA and CFA, and evidence for convergent validity was obtained by examining the correlations between the measures of digital literacy, AI literacy, AI attitude, and collaborative learning skills. The findings provide empirical support for the internal structure and external associations of the HACC Scale, showing that this scale provides a basis for future research and instructional practices aimed at enhancing human–AI collaboration.

items.title: Development of an AI-Based Awkward Working Posture Detection System Using the REBA Method with Edge Computing and Deep Learning Approaches in Industrial Workshops
items.abstract: Awkward working postures pose ergonomic risks in industrial workshops, particularly when combined with force, repetition, or prolonged exposure. This study implements a human-in-the-loop ergonomic assessment system integrating MediaPipe Pose, Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA), and edge computing. A Jetson Orin Nano processes uploaded media and Real Time Streaming Protocol (RTSP) camera streams. MediaPipe estimates 33 body landmarks to calculate six segment angles, while HSE personnel verify landmark placement and task factors before final scoring. The system stores assessment records in MySQL and displays them through a web dashboard. Four workshop postures involving low-workpiece handling, pipe maintenance, grinding, and welding demonstrate system functionality. System-derived REBA scores were 5 for squatting (Case A) and conditionally 5 for bending (Case B). Case B's final score was withheld because wrist visibility fell below 0.50. Observer scores were 7 and 5, respectively, with both cases classified as medium risk. Grinding and welding cases were evaluated without observer comparisons. Segment agreement reached 3/5 for Case A and 5/5 for Case B. During a two-hour RTSP test involving 93,729 frames, mean latency was 74.14 ± 19.64 ms, throughput reached 13.04 ± 2.08 FPS, and CPU/GPU utilization averaged 21.35%/57.71%. Findings demonstrate operational feasibility while identifying hip-landmark placement and occlusion as key sensitivity factors. However, these descriptive results neither establish measurement accuracy nor demonstrate reduced musculoskeletal disorder incidence. Further instrument-based validation across diverse postures and operating conditions remains necessary to establish measurement reliability and broader practical applicability.

items.title: Digital governance of generative AI in higher education: authentic assessment as a pathway to student engagement and educational equity
items.abstract: Universities worldwide are struggling to govern students’ use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), yet it remains unclear whether institutional governance actually shapes meaningful learning. Existing student-level evidence is largely descriptive, and the little inferential work available suggests that mere awareness of AI policies has no effect on student conduct—leaving the effects of governance quality untested. Drawing on procedural justice, self-determination, and digital divide perspectives, this study develops and tests a model in which perceived GenAI governance quality shapes students’ perceptions of authentic assessment, which in turn relate to student engagement and perceived educational equity. Two-wave survey data were collected from 644 undergraduate and postgraduate students across research-intensive, teaching-oriented, and vocational-applied universities in eastern, central, and western China, and were supplemented by objective coding of institutional AI policies. Estimated with institution-clustered standard errors, governance quality was positively associated with perceived authentic assessment well beyond mere policy awareness, more than doubling the explained variance. Authentic assessment fully mediated the relationship between governance quality and student engagement and partially mediated its relationship with perceived educational equity, while digital access remained an independent predictor of equity. Findings indicate that AI governance becomes educationally meaningful primarily when students experience it as authentic assessment, whereas equity additionally requires attention to procedural and resource conditions. Implications for institutional AI policy design are discussed.

items.title: Digital Health implementation experiences among nurses with and without Donor-Funded project affiliation in Kenya: An exploratory cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background Nurses’ participation and continuing support are important dimensions of electronic medical record (EMR) implementation. Evidence comparing these experiences across donor-funded and facility-employed nurses in Kenya is limited. This study compared reported design participation, pilot participation and ongoing training between these groups. Methods This exploratory secondary analysis used a cross-sectional, self-administered nursing survey conducted between March and May 2025. Analyses included 329 nurses: 190 reporting donor-funded project work and 139 identifying as facility employed without donor-funded project work. Design participation was the primary outcome; pilot participation and ongoing training and sensitisation were secondary outcomes. Agreement combined agree and strongly agree responses. Modified Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) with facility-clustered robust standard errors, adjusting for gender, age, education and facility tenure. Sensitivity analyses examined alternative sample definitions and modelling approaches. Results Agreement with design participation was 26.3% among donor-funded respondents and 47.5% among facility-employed respondents; corresponding proportions were 43.7% and 69.8% for pilot participation, and 96.8% and 55.4% for ongoing training. After adjustment, differences in design participation (PR 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.53–1.34) and pilot participation (PR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65–1.16) attenuated. Higher agreement with ongoing training persisted (PR 1.83, 95% CI 1.49–2.26), with consistent findings across sensitivity analyses. All respondents agreed with deployment training. Non-agreement with ongoing training among facility-employed respondents was predominantly neutral. Conclusions Work affiliation was associated with reported ongoing EMR training, while adjusted differences in design and pilot participation remained uncertain. Nursing managers should assess continuing support separately from deployment training and review training opportunities across work affiliations. These exploratory associations do not establish causal effects of employment or donor funding.

items.title: Digital Leadership and Employees' Innovative Work Behavior in Creative Design Enterprises: Evidence from Chongqing, China
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between digital leadership and employee innovative work behavior in AIGC-enabled creative design enterprises in Chongqing, China. It pursues three objectives: to test the direct relationship between digital leadership and innovative work behavior; to examine the mediating roles of STARA awareness, digital work self-efficacy, and digital organizational citizenship behavior; and to assess the moderating role of work autonomy. Grounded in social cognitive theory and social exchange theory, the study proposes that digital leadership is related to innovation through lower AI-related threat, stronger digital confidence, and voluntary digital knowledge sharing, with work autonomy shaping these relationships. A sequential mixed-methods design was used. Semi-structured interviews with 25 employees and managers informed construct contextualization and item wording, followed by a pilot test with 116 valid responses. The main survey obtained 516 valid responses from employees across nine creative design subsectors. Data were analyzed using CFA, SEM, bias-corrected bootstrapping, and hierarchical regression. Results supported all 13 hypotheses. Digital leadership was positively associated with innovative work behavior, digital work self-efficacy, and digital organizational citizenship behavior, and negatively associated with STARA awareness. STARA awareness was negatively associated with innovative work behavior, whereas digital work self-efficacy and digital organizational citizenship behavior were positively associated with it. The three mediation paths jointly accounted for 75.9% of the total effect. Work autonomy buffered the negative STARA awareness–innovation link and strengthened the positive links from digital work self-efficacy and digital organizational citizenship behavior to innovation. These findings extend digital leadership research by identifying a cognitive–capability–citizenship mechanism for innovation in autonomy-supportive AIGC work.

items.title: Digital Tools for the Detection of Dermatitis: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Contact dermatitis (CD) plays a significant role in occupational health due to its frequent occurrence and environmental triggers and is among the most common occupational diseases in Western countries. Despite its prevalence, occupational contact dermatitis (OCD) is often overlooked by occupational physicians, largely due to limited knowledge and a lack of validated detection tools. Advances in digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) offer promising opportunities for improving early detection, yet an overview of available digital tools and their effectiveness in dermatitis detection is lacking. A systematic review was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cinahl, and Scopus. The search focused on original studies published in peer-reviewed journals between 2014 and 2024. Forty-three studies evaluating digital tools for dermatitis detection were included, categorized as models (n = 31) or devices (n = 12). Models represent AI algorithms not yet in practical use, while devices are tools already implemented. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) were the most commonly used computational technique. Median sensitivity and specificity were 0.84 and 0.97 for all tools, 0.85 and 0.97 for models, and 0.78 and 0.97 for devices. The results provided in this review will serve as valuable input for the development of new tools to enhance early OCD detection.

items.title: Digital twins for intelligent intersections: A literature review
items.abstract: Digital twins (DTs) are increasingly proposed as a pathway toward safer, more adaptive, and more efficient intersection management, yet the literature remains conceptually uneven and methodologically fragmented. This review critically synthesizes 99 studies on DTs and closely related DT-enabling systems for intelligent intersections through five analytical dimensions, namely (i) Architectures and Integration Frameworks, (ii) Data Pipelines and Simulation Fidelity, (iii) Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) for Twin-Enabled Traffic Control, (iv) Human-Centered Safety, Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs), and Ethics, and (v) Scaling, Orchestration, and Network Integration. The review adopts a human-curated, multi-source screening and synthesis process in which large language models (LLMs) are used as bounded support tools for note taking, early screening, and draft synthesis, while all final interpretations, categorizations, and claims are validated against the source texts. Beyond summarizing recent work, the paper explicitly distinguishes digital models, digital shadows, and twin-complete systems, showing that many self-labeled transportation “digital twins” exhibit characteristics more consistent with digital shadows or advanced simulators, with only a smaller subset demonstrating operationally coupled twin functionality. The synthesis highlights major advances in modular architectures, multimodal sensing, co-simulation, reinforcement learning, and edge-to-cloud deployment, while also identifying persistent gaps in bidirectional synchronization, validation under real-world uncertainty, VRU-centered design, interoperability, governance, and large-scale deployment. The paper concludes with a sharper research agenda for moving DTs for intelligent intersections from promising prototypes toward operational, trustworthy, and human-centered urban systems.

items.title: Digitalization of Recruitment in Nigerian Public Establishments: Difficulties and Potentials at the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security
items.abstract: Background: Digitalization has greatly transformed HRM all over the world, especially in the field of recruitment. However, Nigerian Public Institutions still experience difficulties in the adoption and implementation of digital recruitment systems. Objective: This study explored the challenges and opportunities of digitalization in the recruitment process in the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, Nigeria. Method: A quantitative case study was used, and data were collected from 30 human resource managers, information technology officers, and recruitment staff using a structured questionnaire given via Google Forms. The questionnaire included technical challenges, human factors, organizational factors, perceived potentials, and digital recruitment effectiveness measured on a 5-point Likert scale. Results: Descriptive results revealed moderate technical, human, and organizational challenges, while perceived potentials of digital recruitment showed higher mean scores ranging from 4.10 to 4.32, particularly for efficiency, transparency, and access to talent. Technical challenges (r = ?0.42) and human factors (r = ?0.35) were negatively correlated with digital recruitment effectiveness, whereas perceived potentials showed the strongest positive relationship (r = 0.85). Regression analysis revealed that perceived potentials had a significant positive effect (? = 0.78, p < 0.001), while technical challenges had a significant negative effect (? = ?0.35, p = 0.007). Conclusion: The findings highlight the need to improve technical infrastructure and strengthen the potential benefits of digital recruitment to facilitate more effective recruitment practices in Nigerian public institutions.
